source.author: ov
source.text: Finitimi proceres coeunt, urbesque propinquae oravere suos ire ad solacia reges, Argosque et Sparte Pelopeiadesque Mycenae et nondum torvae Calydon invisa Dianae Orchomenosque ferax et nobilis aere Corinthus Messeneque ferox Patraeque humilesque Cleonae et Nelea Pylos, neque adhuc Pittheia Troezen, quaeque urbes aliae bimari clauduntur ab Isthmo exteriusque sitae bimari spectantur ab Isthmo.
source.text_original: Finitimi proceres coeunt, urbesque propinquae / oravere suos ire ad solacia reges, / Argosque et Sparte Pelopeiadesque Mycenae / et nondum torvae Calydon invisa Dianae / Orchomenosque ferax et nobilis aere Corinthus / Messeneque ferox Patraeque humilesque Cleonae / et Nelea Pylos, neque adhuc Pittheia Troezen, / quaeque urbes aliae bimari clauduntur ab Isthmo / exteriusque sitae bimari spectantur ab Isthmo.
source.text_english: The neighboring nobles gather, and the nearby cities begged their kings to go to the consolation rites: Argos, Sparta, Pelopid Mycenae, and Calydon, still not hateful to grim Diana, Orchomenos, fruitful Corinth, famous for bronze, fierce Messene, Patrae, humble Cleonae, and Nelean Pylos, and Troezen, not yet Pittheus’ city, and whatever other cities are enclosed by the twin-sea Isthmus, or lie outside it and are seen from the twin-sea Isthmus.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nititur hinc Talaus fratrisque Leodocus urget remo terga sui, quos nobile contulit Argos.
reuse.text_original: nititur hinc Talaus fratrisque Leodocus urget / remo terga sui, quos nobile contulit Argos.
reuse.text_english: From this side Talaus presses on, and Leodocus drives with his oar the backs of his brother’s men, whom noble Argos had brought together.
